name: Foundation Offices

text: A plate beside the door. DIRECTORATE OF WEATHER AND SEA.
Under it a hand-lettered card that has been there long enough to yellow:
IF YOU ARE HERE ABOUT A FORECAST, WE WERE WRONG. COME IN ANYWAY.
The trace wall. Forty-one stations, one roll each, wound off all day.
Six of the coastal rolls have run flat for nine weeks.
A note pinned over them: INSTRUMENT FAULT. SIX AT ONCE? - and no answer.
Storm glasses in a rack, sixty of them, each labelled with a village.
The oldest is from Hearthmere and is forty years old.
Somebody has to look at every one of these twice a day, and somebody does.
A bench of half-built instruments and a ledger of what they cost.
The Foundation gives them away. The ledger records the giving, not the price.
The last entry is a set of nine for a fishing village of two hundred.
A plate beside the door. RELIEF, CONSERVATION AND PUBLIC PROGRAMMES.
A rota is pinned under it with fourteen names on it and every
night of the coming month covered.
Shelves of case files, one per disaster, going back sixty years.
1049. 1052. 1058. 1061. The spines get thinner as they get newer,
because fewer people die in them, because of this room.
Breeding registers for eleven species. Two are marked RECOVERED.
One is marked GONE, in a different hand, and the page after it
is a letter of apology to nobody in particular.
A plate beside the stairs down. FIELD SCIENCES.
Beside it a rack of coats, thirty hooks, and eleven coats.
The other nineteen are somewhere out in the weather right now.
Water tanks under a running tap, and a card of what is in them:
samples from every river mouth in Caelora, taken monthly.
The eastern ones are all stoppered and dated in the same week.
A specimen table. Bones, sorted, labelled, and argued over in pencil
in three hands down the margin of the same card.
The argument is about a joint. It has been going on for two years.
A resonance bench: coils, glass, and a cut Aurelian ring on a stand,
wound about with new copper that is not Aurelian at all.
The card says REPLICA. The ring is not a replica.
A plate beside the door. ANTIQUITIES AND RECORDS.
And below it, the reading rule: NOTHING LEAVES THIS ROOM.
Somebody has added, in pencil, and much older ink: NOTHING EVER HAS.
EXPEDITIONS, A-F. Cloth-bound, one per season, forty years deep.
Every one of them has a crew list in the back, and every crew list
has a column headed RETURNED with a tick or a blank in it.
EXPEDITIONS, G-M. A gap on the shelf the width of two volumes,
with the dust drawn back in a clean rectangle.
The ledger card in the slot says only: WITHDRAWN. DIRECTOR'S OFFICE.
VESSELS AND CHARTERS. Insurance papers, hull surveys, loss reports.
The loss reports are the thinnest bundle here and the most handled.
Every one of them is signed off by an assessor. Every one but one.
FIELD STAFF, PAST. Personal files, alphabetical, and a stool to reach them.
The drawer runs from ABBOTT to FENNIMORE and shuts properly
except at the E's, where something has been put back in a hurry.
ANTIQUITIES, ACCESSIONS. What was dug up, where, and by whom.
The Aurelian entries are the fullest in the room and the most careful,
and almost all of them are in the same small, patient hand.
The reading rules, framed. Requests in writing. Pencil only.
A file may be withdrawn to the Director's office by the Director alone.
Under the frame, a request slip half filled in and then abandoned.
The reading table. A lamp, a blotter, and a jar of sharpened pencils.
Nobody is at it. The chair on the far side has been pulled out
and left out, which in a room with rules like this one is loud.

_plan: The working floor. It has to read as a building full of people doing their jobs well, because it is one. The Elias material is deliberately not written here -- the story agent owns that beat -- but every hook it needs is placed and pointed at: a two-volume gap in EXPEDITIONS G-M withdrawn to the Director's office, a loss report nobody signed off, a personal-file drawer that will not shut at the E's, and a reading chair pulled out and left out. The archive is the bottom-right room, x15-24 / y11-20, reached through the gap at (18,10). The west stair (1,8)/(1,9) is DEEP SURVEY and is closed by one guard on (2,8) plus a parked trolley on (2,9); set aur_deep_open and the guard goes.
